text.content:
Latin name: Via Ossis

Virtues: Conviction, Self-Control

The body is merely a vessel for the soul, or so followers of the Via Ossis believe. Cainites, in their view, are suspended in a vexing state of unlife — not alive as mortals are, but not truly dead either, since they may still think and act. Adherents hold that the physical body passes from birth through life into death while the soul endures, passing into another body oblivious to its prior existence; they do not revere life on an individual basis but as part of this collective cycle, and many conduct sacrifices or experiments in which subjects die so the vampire may study the soul's journey back to its origin. Followers of the Road of the Bones see vampirism itself as a break in this cycle, likening a Cainite to a parasite “borrowing” part of the cycle from the mortals it feeds upon, and most expect (without much eagerness to hasten it) that their own Final Death will return them to the cycle at last. The Road draws its followers primarily from Clan Cappadocian, along with a scattering of morbid @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce}; adherents are typically dispassionate empiricists, seeking a scientific answer to matters of the spirit, though some seek merely to substantiate their faith.

The Ethics:

  • The body is a vessel; only the soul's cycle of death and rebirth truly matters.
  • Study death whenever it presents itself — understanding is only won firsthand.
  • Do not let compassion, fear, or sentiment stay a killing hand when knowledge is to be gained.
  • Share insight into the mystery of death with fellow travelers of this Road.
  • Vampirism is a parasitic interruption of the natural cycle; do not pretend otherwise.

Hierarchy of Sins (most to least severe):

  1. Refusing to kill when the opportunity to study a death presents itself.
  2. Refusing to feed when hungry, or succumbing to frenzy.
  3. Letting compassion sway a decision; acting in a needlessly sacrificial manner.
  4. Needlessly preventing a death; refusing to share insight with a fellow follower of this Road.
  5. Failing to study an occurrence of death; showing fear of, or aversion to, death.

Storyteller/LARP note: The Road of the Bones remains in active use among Cappadocians (and the odd @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce}) throughout the Dark Medieval era. Later editions place its eventual eclipse and rebirth as the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.paths-of-enlightenment.JournalEntry.XaFK1xcneAZ4CbV5]{Path of Death and the Soul} after Clan Cappadocian's destruction — a detail Storytellers running Dark Ages chronicles may treat as distant future history rather than present-day fact.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Cappadocian, Chapter Three: Observations and Conclusions
